[tool: bash]
I wrote `/tmp/obench-cell-q_v3g2s9/bench_opencode_polyglot-rust-c_czf6o8uo/polyglot/main.rs`. It compiles and runs correctly under both `rustc` and `g++ -x c++`. Both give f(0)=1, f(1)=1, f(2)=2, f(10)=89 and f(100)=573147844013817084101.

It uses two tricks:
- **C++ code hidden from Rust:** Rust block comments nest and C++ ones don't. The opening `/* /*` followed by `*/` on the next line therefore leaves the C++ code live for C++. Rust still sees it as a comment, and the closing `// */` ends it.
- **Rust code hidden from C++:** the last line of Rust code follows a `//\` line. C++ splices the backslash line onto the next one, so that code is part of a comment. Rust just sees a plain `//` comment and then the code.

Both versions use 128-bit integers, so they work up to k=185. `g++` may warn about a multi-line comment because of the `//\` line.

`rustc` writes its binary (`main`) to your current directory, not next to the source. Run it from the `polyglot` directory if you want `polyglot/main`.
